newsitem.title: UK: UK peak month car registrations rise 2.2 pct -SMMT.
newsitem.headline: UK peak month car registrations rise 2.2 pct -SMMT.

text.p: British new car registrations rose by just 2.2 perent year-on-year to 479,047 vehicles in the peak sales month of August, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders Ltd said.
Registrations during the first eight months of the year totalled 1,519,175, verus 1,454,097 in the same 1995 period, for a cumulative rise of 4.5 percent, SMMT added.
Ernie Thompson, SMMT chief executive, said "The good news is that we have enjoyed the second highest monthly car market ever.
"The not-so-good news is that the retail market, which has been growing recently at 10 percent, slowed to less than one percent despite a massive marketing campaign by the industry."
Ford's small Fiesta car won the battle for best-seller of the month during which sales traditionally surge on the introduction of the year's new registration index letter.

With 32,650 cars sold in August, the Fiesta outstripped its nearest rival, the small/medium Ford Escort, by about 1,200 cars in the month and the two stablemates are firmly entrenched as the best sellers of 1996 so far with over 100,000 sales each.
